Hi Alex / Marissa —

Thanks again for the renewal discussion earlier this week. As we prep for our upcoming board review, AtlasAI wants to simplify the renewal mechanics so we can reduce admin overhead across multiple teams. Two asks from our side:

1) Move to a single anniversary date for all Redwood services (currently split across Q2 and Q4).
2) Add a defined conversion window in the renewal term where we can exercise an uplift at pre-agreed pricing for any capacity increases (30-day window).

We prefer a 24-month commitment with an annual true-up and the conversion window to avoid re-contracting for small bursts. Attached is our internal projection for Q3 (Q3_capacity_projection.xlsx) to help size the uplift band.

Can you confirm whether the proposed conversion window and consolidated anniversary are workable? If there are material legal/finance implications we should know now, please flag them so we can surface to our CFO. Rajiv (cc) will coordinate procurement.

Thanks —
Elena

Elena —

Appreciate the clear asks and the projection. Short answer: yes, we can support a consolidated anniversary and a 30-day conversion window, but there are a couple of operational items to align on up front so implementation stays smooth:

- Billing cadence: If we re-anchor to a single anniversary, we need to decide whether to prorate the first consolidated invoice or apply credit-based smoothing. Marissa — thoughts on preferred approach from an account ops perspective?
- Commitment term: a 24-month commitment with annual true-ups is generally fine; finance will want the true-up schedule codified in the SOW to avoid ambiguity.
- Conversion window mechanics: We can predefine an "uplift band" (e.g., +10/20/50% tiers) with pre-negotiated unit pricing for 30 days; activation should be possible via API trigger or a signed PO. Connor — can your team confirm if API enablement timeline fits Rajiv's procurement window?

I've attached our standard Master Amendment template (AtlasAI_MA_template_v3.pdf) with the areas we'd update for anniversary date and conversion window. If Atlas signs off on the mechanics, I can draft an amendment and route to legal + procurement for a rapid turnaround.

Next step: if you can confirm the preferred proration approach (credit smoothing vs prorated charge) and whether the uplift tiers in the projection look reasonable, I'll work with Marissa and Neha to capture the SOW language.

Best,

Thanks for the context. From an account ops & billing perspective I recommend the following to minimize friction:

- Use credit smoothing for the first consolidated invoice (apply any remaining Q2 credit to offset the shortened period, then normalize on the new anniversary). This avoids a large one-off prorated charge.
- Lock the uplift band into three discrete tiers (10%, 25%, 50%) with unit price multipliers documented in the SOW. That keeps true-ups simple and avoids per-request pricing negotiations.
- Add a 7-day notice minimum before the end of the 30-day conversion window for API-triggered activations so we have time to provision burst capacity.

If Rajiv can accept standard MA edits (no novel indemnities), we can prepare an amendment; legal review will be fast. Also tagging Neha for pricing confirmation: Neha, do the tier multipliers above align with current discounting matrices for enterprise renewals?

Marissa
